title: Blueprint terms used in this course

table.caption: Glossary
head: Term
Definition
Boundary or example
rows: Blueprint Consultation
Structured sales process connecting use case discovery, workflow/value evidence and executive alignment to a validation decision.
Not a guaranteed pilot or post-sales reference architecture.
Visioning
Outcome-led discovery and prioritization of candidate use cases.
First customer-facing step; duration varies by source/context.
Day-in-the-Life (DITL)
Detailed investigation of a prioritized workflow with practitioners and business/technical owners.
Current work, future hypothesis, time, systems and business consequence.
Playback
Optional review of mapped workflows or targeted future-state demonstration.
Use to resolve a specific uncertainty, not as a mandatory extra loop.
Executive Validation / Readout
Joint value and decision conversation with the customer sponsor and relevant owners.
Stage 3 in referenced motion; sponsor/criteria/path decision.
PBO
Positive Business Outcome: the beneficial business change the customer seeks.
Not merely installing a product or holding a workshop.
Value hypothesis
Source-aware point of view about problem, urgency, solution relevance and potential value to test.
Not a measured result or guaranteed ROI.
Three Whys
Why Change, Why Now and Why Glean.
Customer-specific, linked to evidence and priority.
Use case
A specific actor/job/trigger that may improve a business outcome.
More concrete than improve support.
Workflow
Sequence of actors, steps, systems, inputs, handoffs, decisions and outputs.
Map before proposing automation.
Current state / As-Is
How work happens today with evidence and uncertainty.
Observed, interview-estimated or unknown must be labeled.
Future state / To-Be
Proposed changed workflow and retained controls/dependencies.
Hypothesis until feasibility and outcome evidence support it.
Impact
Business consequence and reach/frequency of an improvement.
May involve cost, revenue, risk or quality; not seats alone.
Effort
Technical, data, integration, security and organizational work required.
Short user request can still imply high effort.
Quick win
High impact and low effort on the standard 2x2.
Requires evidence; unknown feasibility is not automatically low effort.
Strategic bet
High-impact/high-effort use case.
May be phased after readiness or a narrower first wave.
Nice-to-have
Low-impact/low-effort use case.
May be parked behind more relevant priorities.
Deprioritize
Low-impact/high-effort quadrant.
Can be revisited if evidence or strategic priority changes.
Hero use case
A small selected first-wave priority for deeper investigation.
Sources vary on 3–4 versus 3–5; no universal exact-count rule here.
Metric card
Definition, units, cohort, baseline/target, source, owner, timing and caveats.
Used to make success measurable and transferable.
Baseline
Agreed pre-change reference measurement for the defined cohort and period.
A target or peer result is not the baseline.
Success criteria
Pre-agreed measurable and quality conditions for evaluation/decision.
Include owner, evidence and timing.
Active effort
Time a person spends doing the work.
Distinct from elapsed waiting or total cycle duration.
Elapsed cycle time
Wall-clock time from trigger to outcome, including waiting.
Do not automatically monetize it as labor saved.
Adoption fraction
Share of addressable users actively using the scoped workflow/tool.
Separate from event frequency and recapture.
Data coverage
Share of relevant content available/indexed/accessibly in scope.
Method factor needs approved model interpretation; source formula ambiguity flagged.
Efficiency / removable fraction
Share of raw avoidable burden that the solution could remove.
Do not apply twice to already measured savings.
Recapture rate (rho)
Share of saved capacity deliberately converted into useful business output.
Not user adoption or automatic cash saving.
Capacity value
Equivalent value of freed/reallocated work capacity.
Soft-dollar unless specific business/cost action establishes otherwise.
Hard-dollar benefit
Benefit tied to evidenced cost action, such as cancelled spend or a confirmed avoided cost.
Requires actual cost scope and attribution; do not infer from salary-equivalent hours.
Directional value
A hypothesis supported by limited data or benchmarks with caveats.
Pre-sale estimates should not be called realized value.
Telemetry
Platform usage/engagement and related operational signals.
Proves activity/adoption more directly than business attribution.
System of record
Authoritative operational/financial source for a defined metric.
Metric owner confirms definitions and access.
Attribution
Evidence that the intervention contributed to the observed business change.
Before/after change alone may have confounders.
Net ROI
Same-period benefit minus cost, divided by cost.
Specify scope and benefit type; zero cost needs special handling.
Simple payback
Illustrative time for modeled benefit to cover defined investment.
ROI Lab is a simplified first-year benefit/cost illustration, not a full cash-flow model.
Economic Buyer (EB)
Person with authority over the relevant investment decision.
Not automatically the enthusiastic end user or technical champion.
Champion
Customer advocate with influence, relevant engagement and a credible path to the decision process.
Account team assesses evidence, not just enthusiasm.
BVC
Business Value Consulting support for appropriately scoped value engagements.
Internal routing/capacity and thresholds need current confirmation.
MAP
Mutual Action Plan: customer-agreed milestones, owners, dependencies and decision checkpoints.
Different from a seller-only private close plan.
Glean Lab
A curated/sample-data validation experience in the referenced material.
Confirm current approved definition and limitations before offering.
Sandbox
A temporary scoped environment whose current data/access/feature limitations must be confirmed.
Not automatically a production-fidelity proof or universal entitlement.
Pilot / PoC
Separately justified and approved scoped evaluation tied to a buy/no-buy decision.
Readiness score is evidence, not approval.
RACI
Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed responsibilities agreed for a task/decision.
Course template does not override contractual or account ownership.
SCORM 1.2
LMS content/runtime packaging target used in the reference build notes.
Actual runtime support must be tested in the intended Impartner tenant.
SCO
Sharable Content Object launched and tracked by the LMS.
Proposed architecture: one module per SCO ZIP plus separate final-exam ZIP.
Mastery
Minimum assessment score required to pass the configured learning object.
80 is supported by reference build; course-level aggregation is proposed.
Source clearance
Permission/review decision for external or partner distribution of a claim or asset.
Internal authoring access does not imply redistribution rights.
AI-assisted draft
Generated preparation material awaiting factual, technical and publication review.
Never an automatic customer commitment or credential authority.
